blocks.text: INNNEWS - in modern politics, crises often don't start at the border. It starts with words.
For months before the wave of massive migration shook Ceuta at the end of July 2026, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sán appeared as one of the most vocal European leaders defending migration.

While many countries tightened border policy, Sánzil confirmed that migration was necessary to maintain economic growth and sustain Spanish welfare systems that faced demographic challenges due to low birth rates.

The message reached its peak when Elon Musk criticized the regulatory plan of around 500,000 illegal immigrants. Sándner answered with a sentence that soon became a symbol of his political attitudes: Humanity can be honest.
To his supporters, that statement reflects a bold and humanistic leadership. But for his critics, it sent a very clear signal that Spain was an open country for immigrants.

Sántándo not just convey that view through social media. In parliament speeches and international opinion writings, he continued to reject the narrative that migration was a threat to Europe's future.
Instead, he described an open society as a condition for economic prosperity and social sustainability in the 21st century.

This is where the critics start to harden. His opponents argue that the rhetoric serves as a powerful pull factor. The message of Spanish openness is believed to spread widely up to North Africa and form perception that the opportunities for entering Europe through Spain are greater than any other country.

When about 50,000 people broke into Ceuta by the end of July 2026, the crisis that critics had been warned about has finally occurred. Sántner immediately visited the region and called it a violation of Spanish territorial integrity.
But in his explanation, he put a nearly entirely wrong on the human smuggler network and misleading information regarding the Supreme Court's verdict.

What's interesting is that Sánzn doesn't mention the possibility that the political narrative he's been building for months also has a role in forming the expedition of immigrants. There is no reflection on the impact of messages that continue to emphasize the openness of Spain against the current of newcomers.

For the opposition and a number of European leaders, that's exactly where the problem lies. The government recognizes the role of smuggler, disforming, and geopolitical dynamics, but refuses to consider the possibility that his own rhetoric is part of the crisis.
The debate about Ceuta has now progressed beyond the issue of mere migration. It's a test of how much a leader has said about human behavior on a mass scale.

In the eyes of his supporters, Sándner maintains the value of humanity when many countries choose to shut themselves down. In the eyes of his critics, he showed how idealistic rhetoric can produce consequences that can't always be controlled.

In the end, history might not only be judging what's going on at the Ceuta border fence. History will also judge the spoken words long before thousands of people begin to move towards the gates of Europe.
